The case

Chronic disease is managed in general practice.

Hospital trials compete for a narrow, over-researched population. Primary care holds the rest — earlier in the disease course, more representative and already trusted.

A recruitment pool, not a waitlist

Diabetes, hypertension, asthma, COPD and obesity — managed daily, so eligible patients are already on our books.

Continuous records, not snapshots

One clinical platform network-wide, so feasibility counts come from real data.

Metro and regional, one contract

Perth, Bunbury, Busselton, Margaret River, Dalyellup and Albany — plus Fitzroy North in Melbourne. One agreement reaches a diversity of enrolment that single-region sites can't.

Retention through the usual GP

Participants stay with the practice they know. Familiarity and short travel keep them enrolled.

Allied health, same roof

In-house physiotherapy, podiatry and exercise physiology for functional endpoints and lifestyle arms.

GP-owned decision making

Owned by a practising GP — feasibility decisions are clinical, not corporate.

Capability

Clinics ready for protocol work

Purpose-built facilities with the infrastructure most protocols need, as standard.

Trained study team

PIs, sub-investigators, nurses and coordinators with current ICH-GCP.

Dedicated research space

Private rooms for study visits, plus a quiet space for consent.

Pathology & sample handling

Dangerous goods–certified collection, handling and storage, with centrifuge and refrigerated handling. Specimens are couriered to the sponsor's laboratory, ambient or frozen.

Cold chain & IP storage

Monitored, data-logged, access-controlled storage to National Vaccine Storage Guidelines. 4–8°C refrigeration and −20°C to −80°C freezer.

Records, quality & accreditation

RACGP-accredited practices, central clinical governance and audit-ready documentation.

Emergency preparedness

Oxygen and anaphylaxis management at every practice.

For participants

Thinking about taking part in a trial?

A clinical trial tests whether a treatment, vaccine, device or model of care is safe and works. Taking part is your choice.

Voluntary — say no or withdraw any time, with no effect on your usual care.

Written informed consent first, with as much time as you need.

Every study is approved by an independent Human Research Ethics Committee.

Screening checks a study is safe and suitable for you.

No cost for study visits, tests or treatment; travel reimbursement where the protocol provides it.

Your GP stays involved and your usual care continues.

Register your interest

Hear about future studies that may suit you — not a commitment to join. Ask your Brecken GP, or contact clinical.trials1@breckenhealth.com.au / (08) 9791 8133.
